targets.title: Emancipative Values and Non-Violent Protest: The Importance of “Ecological” Effects.
targets.evidence_quote:
The original study uses the World Values Surveys (WVS), rounds 3 to 5. The data
      used in the replication is from the same source as the original study but using
      rounds 6 to 7.
targets.outcome_quote:
Result: The coefficient for SL-Values (Emancipative ‘Climate’) positively impacts the
tendency to non-violent protest (unstandardized regression coefficient = 0.84, T-value
= 9.78). The effect is statistically significant at the 5% level (p = 0.000), two-tailed
test. Consequently, this claim was replicated.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Each of the five claim-specific evaluations explicitly concludes that the claim was replicated, including both multilevel models and the short-term shift model; all concern one original paper.

reasoning: The assigned GUID directly resolves to the complete SCORE report by the supplied team member Esteban Méndez Chacón. Its reference gives 2012, rather than the supplied title’s 2011. It tests the same paper using later WVS waves, a different sample: replication, not reproduction.
